title: Gate FIRST: fail the build on any .sh or .py — Rust, planted known-bad, mutation
description:
WHAT: the first thing that lands in this repo, before any crate is copied. A Rust gate that walks git ls-files and refuses any path matching *.sh or *.py.

WHY FIRST: if the gate lands after the crates, the repo starts dirty and the gate gets weakened to make the build pass. control-plane is the counterexample -- 160 .sh files, 60,467 lines, 29 wired into cron, all accreted because nothing ever said no.

WHY RUST: a shell gate policing shell is self-defeating. This repo has NO carve-out; the exemption list is empty.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. cargo test -p <gate> FAILS on a tree containing a .sh or .py; PASSES on a clean tree. BOTH directions -- an attack-only suite ships an over-strict gate that gets routed around.
2. PLANTED KNOWN-BAD: a fixture tree with one .sh turns it RED; deleting that file turns it GREEN; both asserted in the SAME run.
3. MUTATION: delete the .sh pattern from the matcher and leg 2 must go RED, proving the verdict is attributable to the pattern.
4. Wired into CI AND cargo test, so skipping CI does not skip the gate. Prove wiring by grep WITH a positive control.
5. ANTI-VACUITY: an empty file list is an ERROR (nonzero), never a pass. A gate that scanned nothing reports identically to one that passed.
6. NO-CLAIM: it gates FILE EXTENSIONS. It does NOT prove no crate shells out at runtime via std::process::Command. Name that as uncovered.

title: All 20 crates forbid unsafe (only 2 do today)
description:
WHAT: of 20 extraction crates, only ntm-fleet-monitor and refill-idle-panes declare unsafe_code = "forbid". Measured 2026-08-31 by reading every Cargo.toml.

MISSING: loop-coverage, fleet-monitor, fleet-truth, fleet-reconcile, pane-truth, pane-dispatch-ready, pane-dispatch-fence, pane-oracle-diff, oracle-compare, loop-queue-filter, verify-dispatch, tick-dispatch, reap-finished-panes, dispatcher-deadman, composer-typed, fast-dispatch, loop-driver, loop-tick.

WHY: a substrate we intend to install on other machines carries the guarantee at the crate boundary, not by convention.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. All 20 Cargo.toml carry [lints.rust] unsafe_code = "forbid".
2. cargo build --workspace succeeds with all 20 set. Any crate that FAILS is reported with the exact unsafe construct and gets its own bead -- do NOT drop the lint to reach green. Use /rust-unsafe-code-exorcist.
3. A gate asserts 20 of 20 by reading Cargo.toml, not a doc claim.
4. MUTATION: remove the lint from one crate -> gate RED.
5. NO-CLAIM: forbidding unsafe in OUR crates says nothing about dependencies. State that posture separately.

title: Verify the AGENTS.md crate table against the source, not the descriptions
description:
WHAT: AGENTS.md documents all 20 crates -- what each does and why it exists. The why-lines are derived from Cargo.toml descriptions and LOC counts, NOT from reading all 25,567 lines. AGENTS.md says so in its Honest Limits section; this bead closes that gap.

WHY: a crate table that reads as authoritative but was assembled from metadata is exactly the kind of confident-and-unverified artifact this fleet keeps shipping. Either verify it or keep the disclaimer.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. For each of the 20 crates, read the actual lib.rs/main.rs and confirm the stated purpose matches the code. Report per-crate: CONFIRMED / DIVERGENT / UNCLEAR.
2. Every DIVERGENT row gets AGENTS.md corrected in place.
3. The dependency claim is re-derived: 14 leaves, 6 with one path dep. Any drift is corrected.
4. The unsafe count is re-derived (claimed 2 of 20).
5. When all rows are CONFIRMED, remove that line from Honest Limits. If any stay UNCLEAR, the disclaimer STAYS and names them.
6. NO-CLAIM: confirming a crate does what its description says is not confirming it does it CORRECTLY.

title: Extract 20 fleet crates from control-plane, deps-first, tests intact
description:
WHAT: move 20 crates (25,567 LOC, 18 with tests) from control-plane/crates/ into this workspace.

DEPENDENCY ORDER (measured from each Cargo.toml):
  LEAVES (0 path deps, first): loop-coverage, fleet-truth, fleet-reconcile, pane-truth, pane-dispatch-ready, pane-dispatch-fence, oracle-compare, loop-queue-filter, verify-dispatch, reap-finished-panes, refill-idle-panes, dispatcher-deadman, composer-typed, loop-tick
  DEPENDENT (1 path dep, after their leaf): ntm-fleet-monitor (-> loop-coverage), fleet-monitor, pane-oracle-diff, tick-dispatch, fast-dispatch, loop-driver

ACCEPTANCE:
1. cargo build --workspace --release green, all 20 crates.
2. cargo test --workspace green. Per-crate test counts reported BEFORE and AFTER; the count does not go DOWN. A silently dropped test file is the failure this criterion exists to catch.
3. The .sh/.py gate is already landed and PASSING before the first crate is copied.
4. Each crate builds INDEPENDENTLY (cargo build -p <crate>) -- proves no hidden workspace coupling.
5. State explicitly whether crates were MOVED or COPIED. If moved, control-plane still builds and its consumers were repointed.
6. NO-CLAIM: a green build is not a working orchestrator. It does not prove any lane dispatches.

title: The lifecycle binary: plan -> beads -> bv triage -> OMP dispatch -> verify -> close
description:
WHAT: the actual product. One installable binary that drives a project end to end using OMP agents, not a collection of lanes. Joshua 2026-08-31: "a native rust binary tool that we can install on any of our machines that orchestrates a project from beginning to end through the entire /beads-workflow /planning-workflow /beads-bv process using omp agents."

THE PIPELINE, and the skill governing each stage:
  plan            /planning-workflow   converge in plan-space first (25x cheaper than code-space)
  plan -> beads   /beads-workflow      every bead self-contained with testable AC: run X expect Y
  triage          /beads-bv            PageRank over the DAG; articulation points, not comfortable leaves
  dispatch        /vibing-with-ntm     one bead, owned files, required proof, stop conditions
  verify          /beads-compliance-and-completion-verification   RE-RUN do not read
  close           typed receipt        commit / bead close with cited evidence / structured ack

THE 20 EXTRACTED CRATES ARE THE DISPATCH+VERIFY HALF. The plan/beads/triage half does not exist yet and is the new build.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. One binary, one subcommand per stage, each runnable independently and composably.
2. Every subprocess (tmux/ntm/br/bv/cargo) follows the asupersync 0.4.9 contract: &Cx first, cx.checkpoint() in loops, region-owned tasks, NO detached spawns, kill the process GROUP not the pid, DRAIN both pipes.
3. A timeout maps to a typed TIMEOUT, never to the token a genuinely failing subject produces.
4. END-TO-END PROOF on a real repo: the binary takes a plan, produces beads with acceptance criteria, triages, dispatches to a real OMP pane, and verifies a close by GROUND TRUTH (a commit or a bead close with cited evidence). Not a fixture, not a dry run.
5. Installable: cargo install from this repo puts a working binary on PATH; state its runtime requirements (tmux socket, ntm, br, bv).
6. NO-CLAIM: proving it on control-plane does NOT prove it on another repo. The substrate travels only when proven.
